issues.description: The problem specification and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will not find the expected emptyStock() method and may be confused or forced to rename the method when aligning with the specification or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, add a new emptyStock() method in the template that delegates to clearInventory() to preserve backwards compatibility (e.g., public void emptyStock() { clearInventory(); }).

issues.description: The Stock class method that clears the inventory is named differently between artifacts: the problem statement (and the solution) specify emptyStock(), while the template implementation provides clearInventory(). This naming mismatch can confuse students when mapping the UML/specification to the starter code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper delegating to clearInventory()) so the template matches the problem statement and the solution. Update any usages accordingly.
